claims.gist: Malware is deliberate, unlike vulnerabilities, which are accidental bugs
SCA scanners miss malware because malicious packages usually receive no CVEs
A controlled proxy in front of public registries is the most important control
A seven-day wait before adopting new versions blocks many account-takeover attacks
Lockfiles and hash pinning stop silent swaps of same-version packages
Disable install scripts by default and allow them only for reviewed packages
Use short-lived SSO credentials, not long-lived cloud keys on developer laptops
Most malicious package versions are found and removed within days

thesis: Stop open-source malware with registry gating, release cooldowns, pinning, and limits on install-time code execution.
